The product's operands are the `int32` `offs_token[:, None]` and the `int64` scalar tensor `input_stride_0` (after line 68's cast), so the front end promotes `offs_token` to `int64` (sign extension, exact) and multiplies in `int64`, wrapping; the model writes the promotion as the two `tl.convert` lines above, `offs_token[:, None]` as `.col BLOCK_DIM` (the `[BLOCK_M]` tensor broadcast along a new column axis). The sum with `offs_dim[None, :]` (`.row BLOCK_M`, likewise promoted to `int64`) is the wrapping `int64` one, which does not wrap on covered instances (the offsets are at most `token_num·topk_num·hidden_dim < 2^63`). `input_ptr + …` advances the `*bfloat16` pointer by each lane's `int64` offset, in elements

entries.note: `for i in tl.range(0, topk_num, num_stages=NUM_STAGE)`: the loop from `0` to the `int32` `topk_num`, step `1`, whose induction variable is an `int32` (the promotion of the bounds); it carries `accumulator` (`tile` is new to the body and not used after the loop, SEMANTICS.md, Loops and unrolling). The scheduling keyword `num_stages=NUM_STAGE` (the host's `NUM_STAGE = 1`) changes the order of one program's accesses; a well-behaved model has no two accesses of one program to the same bytes (this one loads its input tiles and stores its output tile, disjoint), so it changes no outcome and the model omits it (SEMANTICS.md, Loops; Performance-only arguments)

entries.note: `tile = tl.load(base_ptrs + i * input_stride_1, mask=mask_token[:, None] & mask_dim[None, :], other=0.0)`. The pointer block: the `int32` induction variable `i` promotes to the `int64` of `input_stride_1` (the cast made it `int64`), and the model writes the promotion and product as the `tl.convert` line and `i64 * s1` above the load (`let i64 := (← tl.convert .i32 .i64 (Tensor.scalar i)).item`), broadcast to every pointer by `bc`; the wrapping `int64` product does not wrap on covered instances. The mask is the conjunction of the two signed comparisons broadcast along the two axes, `mask_token[:, None] & mask_dim[None, :]` — the model's `(mask_token.col BLOCK_DIM).and (mask_dim.row BLOCK_M)`. `other=0.0` is the Python number `0.0`: a `float32` tensor of its own type (`+0.0`, `FloatV.litF32`), converted to the pointer's dtype `bfloat16` — the model's `tl.convert .f32 .bf16 (tl.full … (FloatV.litF32 (FloatV.ofPat 0)))`; the disabled lanes hold `+0.0`
